title: Frequently asked questions
subtitle: Honest and plain — just like in a conversation

items.question: Who do you work with?
items.answer: Companies with a real IT problem who want someone to solve it end to end — trade, services, manufacturing. I work both with companies that have no IT of their own and with those that have an IT person but need an outsider for a specific job.

items.question: How much does it cost?
items.answer: A consultation is 200 PLN net for 30 minutes, a diagnosis 300 PLN net per hour. If a project follows the diagnosis, its cost comes off the quote. Projects are priced by outcome — after a conversation you know up front what you get and for how much, and you pay in instalments.

items.question: I'm not technical — is that a problem?
items.answer: Quite the opposite, that's what I'm here for. I talk to you plainly, without jargon — I explain what's happening and why something is (or isn't) worth doing. You make the business decisions, I take responsibility for the work.

items.question: Who owns the data and hardware?
items.answer: You do. I work as a consultant — the server, database and hardware are and remain your property. I also leave documentation behind, so anyone else can work on it after me.

items.question: How fast do you respond?
items.answer: I reply to a request within 24 hours, usually the same day. That's response time, not repair time — on first contact I tell you what's going on and when the fix will realistically land.

items.question: Do you work remotely or on-site?
items.answer: Mostly remotely — it's faster and cheaper. But when the server under the desk needs a physical look, or a training has to happen on-site, I come over. I work across Poland.

items.question: What if my problem isn't your thing?
items.answer: I'll say so straight. If I'm not the right person, I'll admit it honestly and — if I can — point you to someone who can help. I'd rather lose the job than your time and trust.

items.question: How do we start?
items.answer: Write two sentences about what's going on. I'll reply within 24 hours and tell you whether a consultation is enough or a diagnosis is needed — and if it isn't my kind of work, I'll say so.
